title: Building One O'Clock Jump at the Reno Club
summary: Basie asked Smith to add something when he changed key from F to D-flat; Smith built the saxophone riffs and the band added others.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I know the story of how it was made.
Yeah, you know how it was made?
Well, you had to find a signature tune or something, and you were playing... Well, you tell the story, because maybe I don't remember exactly.

Basie always...he's always experimenting on something. You see, I played first also. He always relied on me to add something to it, make something out of it. So he started playing blues in F. You know, we mostly played a whole lot of heads down there in the Reno Club -- we only had about eight pieces down there. So he said, "I want to play a little blues..." He called me Prof. He said, "I want to play a little blues in F here, and then I'm going to D-flat." He said, "You put something to it."
You mean, he was telling you this while he was playing in F?
Oh, before he started he said, "I'm going to play down a couple of choruses in F, and then I want you come in D-flat."
Yes. "Put something to it, set something to it, add something to it, and make the cats fall in." I said, "I will. You wait until you get to D-flat; I'll set up something."
Did you have an idea at that stage what you wanted to do?
You knew what you wanted to do.

Yeah. All that I wanted to do was just change keys. If he didn't change keys, I would have said something. But put the D-flat so it would sound weird(?), and get that beautiful tone. And I put the alto just right. And the other cats all fall in underneath there, with the harmony and everything. So we played the first night, and everybody, even the boss man, said, "You all play that tune that the band ...(?). . . jumpin' them keys." He said, "You all play that again." We had to play it three or four times a night. I set them saxophone riffs, until I could tell ...(?). . . and you'd tell them where to go to. Whether to put it in there with the ...(?). . . or whatever you wanted to put in there. Hot Lips was playing first trumpet, but we had Joe Keys on first trumpet. I said, "Lips, you set a little riff there for the trumpets and everything." So we just built it on up like that. So Jack Washington got to raise his hand and he's trying to find his note...
